We cannot easily call because many internal classes.

Thus easiest: use reflection to set private fields in JsonSchema instance: maybe fields "evaluationPath" (type JsonNodePath) and "schemaNode" (type JsonNode). Let's assume names: "evaluationPath" and "schemaNode". We'll set them.

Could use reflection to set evaluationPath to a mock that returns toString path string. But getEvaluationPath() returns a string? Actually in toString they call getEvaluationPath() which likely returns a string representation (maybe path string). So we can mock JsonSchema subclass that overrides getEvaluationPath() and getSchemaNode().

Simpler: create anonymous subclass of JsonSchema that overrides those methods to return desired values. Since JsonSchema is not final. We'll create a subclass TestJsonSchema extends JsonSchema with overridden methods.

But JsonSchema has many abstract methods? It extends BaseJsonValidator which may be abstract but JsonSchema implements many methods. However we can create subclass with constructor that calls super? No-arg constructor maybe exists (default). We can instantiate JsonSchema normally then use Mockito spy to stub getEvaluationPath() and getSchemaNode().

We can use Mockito.spy(schema) and then when(schemaSpy.getEvaluationPath()).thenReturn("/properties/name"); when(schemaSpy.getSchemaNode()).thenReturn(node). Need to ensure methods are not final. They are probably protected or public. getEvaluationPath() is defined in BaseJsonValidator as protected? Not in provided code but used. We'll assume it's protected method accessible via spy.

Thus we can create a JsonSchema instance via factory as before (any schema) then spy and stub.

For cases where schemaNode is null, we need to stub getSchemaNode() to return null and expect NullPointerException.

- private static ObjectMapper mapper = new ObjectMapper();

- helper method createSchemaSpy(String path, JsonNode node) returns JsonSchema.

Implementation:

JsonSchemaFactory factory = JsonSchemaFactory.getInstance(SpecVersion.VersionFlag.V202012);
JsonSchema base = factory.getSchema("{}"); // dummy
JsonSchema spy = Mockito.spy(base);
Mockito.doReturn(path).when(spy).getEvaluationPath();
Mockito.doReturn(node).when(spy).getSchemaNode();

Return spy.

Now test cases:

Group 1 basic concatenation scenarios:

Case1 expected "/properties/name" : {"type":"string"}

Create node = mapper.readTree("{\"type\":\"string\"}");
path = "/properties/name";

expected string: "\"/properties/name\" : " + node.toString();

Call spy.toString() and assertEquals.

Case2 expected "" : true (empty path). Path empty string? The evaluation path empty. So getEvaluationPath() returns "" (empty). Node BooleanNode.TRUE.

Create node = BooleanNode.TRUE (from JsonNodeFactory.instance.booleanNode(true));

expected "\"\" : true". Note quotes around empty string.

Case3 expected "/items[0]/$ref" : [1,2,3] . Path with special chars. Node array.

Create array node = mapper.readTree("[1,2,3]");

expected "\"/items[0]/$ref\" : " + arrayNode.toString();

Case4 expected exception NullPointerException. Stub getSchemaNode() to return null. Path any (maybe "$").

Call spy.toString() and assertThrows NullPointerException.

Group 2 diverse data type handling:

Various cases: we will create nodes accordingly.

Case description: "/description" : "A \"quoted\" description"

Node is TextNode with value A "quoted" description. Using mapper.readTree("\"A \\\"quoted\\\" description\"") yields TextNode.

expected "\"/description\" : " + node.toString();

Case "/price" : 19.99 numeric DecimalNode.

Node = mapper.readTree("19.99")? That's a numeric node (DoubleNode). expected.

Case "/nullNode" : null

Node = NullNode.instance.

Case "/unicode/π" : {"type":"number"}

Node = mapper.readTree("{\"type\":\"number\"}");

Case "/space path/with spaces" : true

Node Boolean true.

Case '"null" : 42' where evaluation path is null (Java null). So getEvaluationPath() returns null. In concatenation, ("" + null) results "null". toString returns ("\""+null+"\"")? Actually code: ("\"" + getEvaluationPath()) + "\" : " + getSchemaNode().toString();

If getEvaluationPath() returns null, then "\""+null gives "null". Then + "\" : " etc results "null\" : 42"? Wait: "\""+null => "null". Then + "\" : " => "null\" : ". So final string starts with "null" without opening quote? Actually initial part: ("\"" + getEvaluationPath()) results in string starting with double quote then evaluationPath. If evaluationPath null, then it's "\""+null => "null". This yields "null". Not with opening quote. Then + "\" : " adds a quote and colon. So final: "null\" : 42". But expected in test case is '"null" : 42' (quotes around the word null). That matches: "null" (with quotes). Let's compute: "\""+null => "null". That's not with quote. Wait string literal "\""+null results in "\""+String.valueOf(null) => "\"null". Because String concatenation: "\""+null => "\""+ "null" => "\"null". So it becomes "\"null". That's a double quote then null. So we have "\"null". Then + "\" : " adds another quote then colon: "\"null\" : ". So final: "\"null\" : 42". That's exactly expected. Good.

Thus we set path null and node numeric 42.

Case "/escaped\\backslash" : false

Path contains backslash. Need to represent path string with single backslash; in Java string we escape as "\\". Node Boolean false.

expected "\"/escaped\\\\backslash\" : false". Because when toString prints path, it will include backslash as is, but in expected string we need double backslash to represent a single backslash in string literal. We'll compute expected via String concatenation.

Group 3 exception propagation:

Case custom toString failure IllegalStateException.

We need a JsonNode mock where toString throws IllegalStateException with message "custom toString failure". Use Mockito.mock(JsonNode.class); when(node.toString()).thenThrow(new IllegalStateException("custom toString failure"));

Stub getSchemaNode() to return that mock. Path any.

Call schemaSpy.toString() and assertThrows IllegalStateException and check message.

Similarly for RuntimeException.

Note: getSchemaNode() is probably protected method, but spy can stub protected using Mockito.doReturn? Might need to use when(spy.getSchemaNode()).thenReturn(node) but if method is protected, we need to use Mockito.doReturn(node).when(spy).getSchemaNode(); This works.
